messages:
Maria: FYI, seeing sporadic token stream stalls from us-east GPU pool this morning. Some streams hit our 2s RPC deadline; others pause ~200-700ms then resume. Affects continuous-batching models on the g4-like nodes in us-east1-b/c.
Ajay: Any packet captures or TCP stats so we know if it's retransmits vs out-of-order?
Maria: Quick tcpdump sample from one affected pod (trimmed):
```
14:10:22.001234 IP 10.20.3.11.60000 > 10.20.7.5.443: Flags [.], seq 1000:1400, ack 9000, win 64240
14:10:22.001400 IP 10.20.7.5.443 > 10.20.3.11.60000: Flags [.], ack 1400, win 32100
14:10:22.001610 IP 10.20.3.11.60000 > 10.20.7.5.443: Flags [.], seq 1400:1800, ack 9000, (reordered)
```
Maria: Kernel counters show elevated TCP reordering and SACKs on those hosts.
Noah: Reordering + GRO can trick the TCP stack into delivering segments out of order before reassembly. Did we roll any kernel or driver updates last night?
Sam: We pushed a minor kernel bump from 5.15.11 -> 5.15.14 across the pool at 02:00. NIC firmware was unchanged. We also enabled 9000 MTU on the host image recently.
Ajay: Mixed MTU across path + ECMP path asymmetry could cause this. If some spine switches still use 1500 for the spillover VLANs, large segments may be fragmented or encapsulated and arrive reordered. Also vendor NIC drivers have known GRO reordering bugs with that kernel.
Maria: Confirmed: host MTU = 9000, but a couple of adjacent spine ports report 1500 on their management VLAN -> mismatch possible for some flows during failover.
Noah: For immediate triage we should try toggling off host offloads and run a canary. Commands:
```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_reordering=3
```
Sam: Lower blast radius: pick 4 nodes, disable offloads, run 1k short streaming requests, measure p50/p95/p99 token latency + SACKs. If tail drops, we likely have GRO/driver bug.
deploy-bot: @Maria started canary job streaming-reorder-triage-1768610000 (canary nodes: 4). Logs: https://internal/logs/streaming-reorder-1768610000
Maria: Canary results after disabling GRO: p95 streaming tail from 480ms -> 55ms, SACKs drop to near-zero on canary hosts. CPU on nodes increased ~4%.
Noah: Strong signal. Next steps: open vendor case with pcap + dmesg + NIC stats. If vendor concurs, either firmware roll or keep offloads disabled in our golden image until fix.
Ajay: I've opened ticket INC-2026-378 with vendor, attached capture and kernel/driver versions. Also preparing a temporary routing tweak to prefer AZ-local spine for affected cohorts for 6 hours to reduce ECMP churn while we triage.
Sam: Note cost/perf tradeoff: disabling offloads raises CPU on worker pods and may reduce throughput. FinanceOps, flagging possible short-term need to increase capacity by ~6% to keep SLA headroom.
FinanceOps: Acknowledged. Please include estimated hours and projected spend impact in the postmortem.
Maria: Plan for next 24h: keep offloads disabled on affected 8% cohort, watch token latency, schedule vendor debug session. If vendor suggests rollback, we'll roll firmware on small batches. I'll post an update in #eng-runtime in 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
